role.altitude: The electronics engineer keeps presenting, negotiating, setting targets and debugging prototypes; collecting results, typing readings and formatting slides and notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping a position list and a test data store that the drafting steps can use
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who compares more design variants before building a board.

tasks.short: Read the agenda and other members' contributions, pull supporting test results, write the slides and a position note, get them cleared, present and negotiate at the meeting, and report back what was agreed.

steps.what: Electronics engineer reads the agenda, previous minutes and other members' contributions or draft documents

loop.input: The agenda, each contribution or draft document, and the engineer's position list (the clauses and topics the company cares about).
loop.output: Per contribution: the clauses or topics it changes that are on the position list, each with the quoted source passage and its location.
loop.check: Every quoted passage must be found word for word at the stated location, or the item is dropped; contributions the step cannot read are listed for the engineer; the engineer opens the original for every flagged item.
loop.stop: One pass per document; no re-runs on the same version.
loop.why_not_simpler: A version compare works for a revised draft, but most contributions are free-text proposals with no earlier version to compare against.

steps.what: Electronics engineer pulls the test results and calculations that support the company's findings into charts
Electronics engineer writes the slides and a position note that says what the company can and cannot accept

loop.input: The engineer's outline of the argument, the supporting charts with their run ids, and the house slide template.
loop.output: Draft slides with headings, short text and the charts placed; the position note is written by the engineer.
loop.check: Every number on a slide must match a value in the supporting charts' data, and each slide's statement must say what its chart shows and what the outline point says, or the slide is marked for the engineer; claims not in the outline are removed; the engineer edits every slide.
loop.stop: One draft per outline; if the engineer rejects it, the engineer writes the slides.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template gives layout and charts, not the short wording of each argument.

steps.what: Engineering manager reviews the final presentation and position note for confidential content and the negotiating limits, and clears both
Electronics engineer presents and explains the findings at the conference, committee or working group and answers questions
Electronics engineer defends the recommendations, negotiates compromises within the mandate and exchanges information with other members
Electronics engineer writes the meeting report for colleagues with what was actually agreed, open points and actions

loop.input: The engineer's own meeting notes and, when issued, the official minutes of the meeting.
loop.output: Draft report: decisions taken, compromises agreed, open points and actions with owners.
loop.check: Every decision and action must match a line in the engineer's notes or the official minutes and say the same thing, with the same owner and conditions, or it is dropped; items the notes and minutes describe differently, or that the notes do not mention, are flagged for the engineer; the engineer edits the draft.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; a rejected draft means the engineer writes the report.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes are free text; a template gives the report headings, not what was agreed.

steps.what: Electronics engineer checks the final report before posting: each agreed point and action says what was agreed, and the project space and readers are the right ones
Electronics engineer posts the checked meeting report in the project space for colleagues

approvals.approved_version: presentation, final version as cleared in s4; any later edit voids the clearance
position note, final version as cleared in s4 (the negotiating mandate); a compromise beyond it needs a new clearance

The meeting report with agreed points, open points and actions with owners exactly as checked by the engineer in s7b, posted once to the project's space in {DOCS} for the project colleagues; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Agendas and contributions sit in {DOCS}; a bounded step lists, per contribution, the clauses on the engineer's position list with quoted passages, and the engineer reads the flagged originals. An artefact generator draws charts from the chosen runs in the {OTHER} lab test data store, and a bounded step drafts slides from the engineer's outline with every number checked against those charts. The manager clears the final slides and position note; presenting, defending and negotiating stay with the engineer, and afterwards a bounded step drafts the meeting report from the engineer's notes and the official minutes; the engineer checks the final report and posts it once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contributions arrive as free text in many formats, and test results sit in personal spreadsheets, so every preparation started from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models can summarise long technical documents with quotes that can be checked word for word; chart generators can read a lab data store.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room, defending a position under questions and judging which compromise the company can live with.
tasks.human_edge: Credibility with peers from other companies and the judgement to trade one clause for another in the room.
tasks.altitude: Preparation shifts from collecting and formatting to sharpening the argument; the meetings themselves do not change.

reach.task: Prepare the company position for customer design reviews
reach.learn: Whether contribution summaries with quotes catch the clauses that matter to the product.

evidence.claim: Language models can summarise technical documents and quote the source passages, so each quote can be checked against the original.
In an experiment with 453 professionals (no engineers), access to a chat model cut writing time by 40% and raised quality by 18%.
Technical data shared with members from other countries can fall under EU dual-use export rules, so disclosure needs a check before the meeting.

assumptions: Boundary: from the meeting agenda to the posted meeting report; travel booking, expense claims and the company's formal vote or signature on an agreement are outside.

Input contract for s2: test results in the {OTHER} lab test data store with run id, conditions, measured values and limits; producer is the test engineer who logs the run; fallback is the engineer exporting the spreadsheet run table into the generator's import sheet.
Input contract for s1: the engineer keeps a position list of clauses and topics; without it the summary step lists all changed clauses.
The meeting report records what was actually agreed, from the engineer's notes and the official minutes, not the planned position.
Coverage: about 70% of meetings are recurring working groups or reviews with contributions in readable files and results in the data store; savings in s1 and s2 are priced at that share.

The manager's review time does not change; in-person presenting and negotiating keep their full time. Writing slides and the position note keeps 80 because the engineer writes the outline and the position note; the draft gives layout, charts and short wording. The meeting report keeps 70 because the engineer still edits what was agreed; checking and posting it keep their full time.
unknowns: How many external meetings per year the engineer attends and how many need slides.
Whether lab results are already in a shared data store or in personal spreadsheets.
research_questions: How often does the contribution summary miss a clause the engineer later finds important?
How much of the drafted slide text is kept?

already_counted.description: Electronics engineer opens the originals for flagged items in the contribution summaries.
Electronics engineer picks the test runs and checks the generated charts.
Electronics engineer edits the drafted slides and fixes flagged numbers.
Electronics engineer edits the drafted meeting report and checks flagged minute items.

incremental.description: Electronics engineer keeps the position list current after each meeting.
Electronics engineer maintains chart definitions when the test data fields change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of meetings have readable contributions and results in the data store, so s1 keeps 82 and s2 keeps 58 (13.0); high: about 70% of meetings covered as assumed (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search literature, patents and efficiency rules, set target specifications, design and simulate circuits, build and measure a prototype, analyse results against targets, and write a technical note.

steps.what: Electronics engineer searches papers, patents and product efficiency rules for the green technology topic

loop.input: The engineer's research question and the papers, patents and rule texts retrieved from the {OTHER} literature and patent databases.
loop.output: A summary per question with the reported results, each tied to a paper or patent and page.
loop.check: Every statement must cite a document in the retrieved set and a page, and the cited sentence or table must give the same figure under the same conditions, or the statement is dropped; statements whose conditions or limits are unclear are flagged; the engineer reads the cited sections before using a figure.
loop.stop: One summary per question and retrieved set; a new set means a new run.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search finds documents but does not pull the reported efficiency figures and conditions out of free text.

steps.what: Electronics engineer sets the concept and target specifications such as efficiency, standby power and cost
Electronics engineer designs the circuit and runs circuit and thermal simulations in the design tools
Lab technician assembles the prototype board from the released design
Electronics engineer brings up and debugs the prototype on the bench
Electronics engineer sets up the bench, probes the prototype, runs the efficiency, power and output measurements and starts the logging script

Electronics engineer records the readings: typed from the instrument displays into the run sheet today; after the change instruments with a remote interface log them through the logging script into the lab test data store, and the engineer checks the first readings of each set-up and types the rest
Electronics engineer compares measured results with targets and simulations and works out why they differ
Electronics engineer writes the technical note with method, results, conclusions and next steps and files it

loop.input: The measured results and simulation tables with run ids, the engineer's results analysis, and the note template.
loop.output: Draft method and results sections with tables; conclusions and next steps are written by the engineer.
loop.check: Every number in the draft must match a value in the measured or simulation records by run id, and each result sentence must state what that run shows under its conditions and limits, or it is marked; the engineer edits every section and writes the conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft per note version; if rejected, the engineer writes the sections.
loop.why_not_simpler: The template fills tables, but the method text must describe what was actually set up on the bench.

tasks.design: A literature desk over the {OTHER} paper and patent databases summarises reported figures with page citations that are checked before use. Simulation sweeps defined in a parameter table run as an overnight batch in the design tools, and bench instruments with a remote interface log readings straight into the {OTHER} lab test data store. A dashboard compares measured values with targets and simulations, and a bounded step drafts the method and results sections of the technical note from those records; the engineer writes conclusions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings were typed from instrument displays into spreadsheets, and reported figures had to be dug out of papers by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Most current bench instruments accept remote commands, and language models can extract figures from papers with checkable page citations.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing which idea to pursue and finding why a prototype misses its target; simulation set-up by a model is not reliable enough to trust.
tasks.human_edge: Judging which green technology idea is worth building and diagnosing why a prototype underperforms.

ambition.what: Compare more design variants by overnight simulation sweeps before committing to a prototype board.

tasks.altitude: The engineer spends less time typing readings and formatting notes and more time on design choices; decision rights do not change.

reach.role: electro-mechanical and mechatronics technologists and technicians
reach.learn: Which bench set-ups log reliably without a person reading the display.

evidence.claim: Bench instruments with a remote interface can be scripted to take and log readings without a person reading the display.
In a multiphysics benchmark the best model strategy produced executable simulation calls 88% of the time, and executable does not mean correct, so simulation set-up stays with the engineer.
EU ecodesign and energy labelling rules set efficiency and standby limits for products such as lighting and televisions.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to the filed technical note; parts and board orders run through purchasing, and patent filings and publications are separate tasks.

Input contract for s6: instruments with a remote interface write run id, set-up, measured value and unit into the {OTHER} lab test data store; producer is the logging script started by the engineer; fallback is the engineer typing readings into the run sheet.

Coverage: about 80% of readings come from instruments with a remote interface; recording readings (s6b) keeps 30: typing for the other 20% plus checking the first logged readings of each set-up. Setting up, probing and running the measurements (s6) and bring-up keep their full time.
Measured results are the actual logged readings, not the planned test values in the target specification.
Input contract for s3: sweeps run only from a parameter table the engineer writes; about half of simulation time is repeated sweeps, so s3 saves about 10%.
The lab technician's assembly time does not change.

Comparing results (s7) keeps 70: the dashboard removes building the comparison tables, while working out why results differ stays. The technical note (s8) keeps 75: the draft fills method and results from records, and the engineer edits them and writes the conclusions.
unknowns: Which bench instruments in the lab have a remote interface.
Whether the company has access to paper and patent databases.
research_questions: How often does a cited figure in the literature summary turn out wrong or out of context?
How many design variants are compared before and after overnight sweeps?

already_counted.description: Electronics engineer reads the cited sections before using a figure from the literature summary.
Electronics engineer checks the first logged readings against the instrument display for each new set-up.
Electronics engineer edits drafted method and results sections and fixes marked numbers.

incremental.description: Electronics engineer adapts logging scripts when bench instruments or set-ups change.
Electronics engineer maintains sweep parameter tables and the note template.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of readings come from remote-capable instruments, so s6b keeps 56, and no sweeps repeat, so s3 keeps 100 (11.2); high: 80% of readings logged and half of simulation time in repeated sweeps as assumed (15.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
